claims.behaviour: Every grid panel has a header (accessible name 'Panel header'): on the left the structure selector and the controls of the chosen source, on the right, in this order, the buttons Run effectors, Pin, Transformations, Quick transformations, Search, Hide items (two-panel mode) and the view selector. The tooltip / accessible label of each: Run effectors = 'Run all effectors in this structure' / 'Run effectors'; Pin = 'Pin focused item to show only its sub-items and parent items' / 'Pin'; Transformations = 'Transformations – sort, filter, group or extend the displayed structure (without changing it)' / 'Transformations'; Quick transformations = 'Quick transformations' for both; Search = 'Search / filter the displayed structure' / 'Search'. The view selector's label is 'View selector'; the structure selector's is 'Structure selector'.

A panel's header wires up its behaviour once, the first time that panel becomes visible, not when the page loads: a secondary panel that was never shown has no search, no restored search state and no structure list request until it is first shown.

On a board or project page the full header is used. In a gadget, on the Jira issue page and on a Jira Software board tab the widget runs as a single panel: no transformations banner, no quick transformations banner, no search banner and no recent-items warning exist there, and their controls do nothing. On the issue page and a Jira Software tab the main Pin, Transformations, Quick transformations, Search and two-panel buttons are removed, and on the Jira Software tab the view selector too. In place of them an issue-and-tab toolbar is added to the right side (see claim ph-issue-toolbar). The search and filter controls are only made functional on the board and project pages.

On the issue page and the Jira Software tab the header's right side starts with: a paste button (tooltip 'Insert current issue after the focused item in the structure'), a pin button (tooltip 'Pin current issue in the structure to show only its sub-items and parent items') and a '...' menu with three sections: 'Add New…'; 'Expand all', 'Collapse all'; 'Edit', 'Copy', 'Cut', 'Paste', 'Remove'. A menu entry performs the same grid action as the toolbar entry of that name; it is greyed out and aria-disabled exactly while that action is unavailable.

On the issue page and the Jira Software tab the paste button is shown only while nothing is pinned, and loses focus when clicked. On the issue page, once the current issue's key is known, the button also shows the text 'Place <issue key>' (for example 'Place ABC-1'). On the Jira Software tab it has no text.

Whenever the panel's forest spec changes: Pin, Transformations, Quick transformations and Search are shown only when the spec is transformable, that is, a valid spec which is not the clipboard. The two-panel button is shown only in the secondary panel and only when the spec is transformable. The transformations list is hidden likewise. While the transformations banner is locked these visibility rules are not re-evaluated, but the pressed state of the two transformation buttons still is.

The Transformations button appears active exactly when the current spec has at least one transformation. The Quick transformations button appears active exactly when at least one of them is a quick transformation. Otherwise each appears as a plain subtle button. Clicking either one toggles the visibility of its banner (transformations banner, quick transformations banner).

The Pin button shows as pressed exactly when the spec has a pinned item, and clicking it runs the grid's toggle-pin action. It belongs to the controls that warn when automation editing mode is on (see claim automation-warning-popup).

When the structure info arrives: the view selector is shown only when the info is an object (not null). The transformations list and search banner are shown only for an object info and a transformable spec; the search banner also needs search or filter mode to be on. The search banner's Save link is shown only if the panel is administrable by the user.

The view selector shows the name of the base view, and a mark '*' (tooltip 'You have adjusted this view and the changes have not been saved on the server yet.') while the view is adjusted. Its tooltip for a view with an id below 0 is just that view's description; for any other view it is 'Current view: <name>' followed by ' - <description>' when there is a description. An unknown view gives an empty name.

On the board and project page the view selector drops its name and shows only the icon when the room left beside the right-hand buttons (panel width minus toolbar width) is less than the width the source controls want: the larger of 100 and (selector label width + 1 + 180 when a query or tool source is chosen, or + the width of the description and archived controls when a structure is shown). On the issue page and Jira Software tab it always shows only the icon. Controls are laid out again whenever that room changes.

The Run effectors button is shown only when the structure info says `effectorExecutionAllowed`. It is disabled unless all of these hold: the panel shows a structure with no transformations and no pinned item, not in a gadget, effector execution is allowed, and the forest holds at least one effector row. The disabled state is recomputed on each forest update and spec change. Clicking when enabled runs the 'Run all effectors' action; when disabled it does nothing.

For a structure, the description banner (with an info icon) above the grid shows the structure's `descriptionHtml` as HTML. With no description it shows 'There is no description...' and the banner is hidden automatically; the user can still open it with the description button or keys `d`,`d`.

Whether a non-empty description shows when a structure is opened is decided in this order: the choice this browser remembered for that structure id (true or false, kept without expiry); else the value already fetched during this page's life; else `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/description-shown`, whose `descriptionShown` is used and kept for the page. A failed request means not shown, and that failure is not kept, so the next change of structure info asks again.

The description button (tooltip and label 'Show structure description') is shown whenever a structure's name is displayed, and shows as pressed while the banner is open. Clicking it or pressing `d`,`d` flips the banner and remembers the new state in this browser for that structure id. This does nothing when the panel has no structure id. Closing the banner with its close control remembers 'not shown' for that structure.

When the bootstrap config (`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`) has a `globalError` text, the panel shows it as plain text in an error banner at the top, order 0, before all other banners. Without one, there is no banner.

Banners above the grid are stacked by order: 0 global error, 1 description, 2 generation stopped, 3 insertion limits and infinite-update loop, 4 search. Their remembered open or closed state is held under the model names `ph.global-error`, `ph.description`, `ph.stop`, `ph.limits`, `ph.infinites`, `ph.search`.

Clicking the Search button toggles search mode, empties the query in both directions and records the statistic `search.toggle` through `POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/record`. Turning search on opens the search banner and moves the keyboard focus into its query box.

The search banner holds, left to right: the query type button (showing 'Text', 'JQL' or 'S-JQL', default 'Text'), a filter button (tooltip 'Filter - don't show non-matching items'), the query box, and a 'Save' link. The type button opens a menu with exactly the entries Text, JQL, S-JQL. Choosing one changes the type, updates the button, moves focus to the box, passes the type to a filter being edited (clearing its error) and, in search mode, reruns the search at once.

In search mode with a valid query, the grid's matches are recomputed 500 ms after the last change of the query. When search is off or the query is empty, the matches are cleared, also after that 500 ms settling. A query with a validation error clears the matches and no search runs until it is fixed.

A search does not call a dedicated REST method: it takes a copy of the panel's current forest spec, appends one transformation {`key`: `filter`, `module`: the filter module for the query type, `params`: {<type>: <query>, `hard`: true}} (the type being `text`, `jql` or `sjql`) and gives that spec to the grid's row filter, which obtains the matching rows. The panel's own spec is unchanged. An unknown query type or an empty query means no filter.
When the panel's spec changes while search mode is on, the search is run again against the new spec at once (unless the transformations banner is locked).

After each search, when the results are ready and the focused row does not match, focus moves to the nearest matching row of the displayed rows, or, when there is none or the focused row is not displayed, of all expanded rows. Nearest means the smaller row distance from the focused row; on a tie the row after it wins. With no match at all focus stays. The search does not scroll for this beyond what focusing a row does.

Keys: Ctrl+Alt+/ turns search on if neither search nor filter is on; if on, moves focus to the box; when the box already has focus it cycles the type Text, JQL, S-JQL, Text. Ctrl+Alt+; and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+/ press the filter button if it is visible. Both are inactive on the issue page and the Jira Software tab. Pressing Enter in the query box removes focus from it, leaving the query in place.

When the search banner asks to cancel its mode (the Esc key while it has focus) and search or filter is on, that mode is closed the same way as the banner's close control, and the event goes no further.

Pressing the filter button while the search is on turns the current query into a real filter transformation: a filter is added to the transformations list with the query and type (the transformations banner becomes its owner, and it counts in the spec), filter mode replaces search mode, and the query box keeps focus. A disabled filter button does nothing.
Pressing the filter button while filter mode is on removes that filter transformation and returns to search mode with the same query and type.
In filter mode a query change reaches the filter transformation 500 ms after the last change, a type change at once (with its error cleared), and a change of the error state at once.

The search banner offers a close control always, and a hide control only in filter mode. Hide leaves filter and search mode but keeps the filter transformation applied. Close in filter mode leaves both modes and removes the filter transformation; in search mode it just turns search off.

Clicking 'Save' in the search banner, when not disabled, opens the generator edit dialog in quick-transformation mode for the current query's filter module with its params as JSON text. On confirmation the filter is added as a quick transformation with the name given in the dialog; the dialog's internal fields are not stored in the params. Cancelling adds nothing.

While transformations are disabled (automation editing mode): the filter button, Pin, the query type button and 'Save' are aria-disabled; an active filter mode is left, keeping its transformation. The transformations banner is disabled too.

The search state of each panel is remembered: either off or the pair query and type. Restored on the next load on all pages but gadgets. Restoring a non-empty query does not take keyboard focus. In the browser it is per panel, not per structure or user: stored without expiry, or, while a shared perspective is open, for the browser session under that perspective.

A shared perspective keeps the header state in its panel part (`primary` or `secondary`) under `panelHeader`: `panelHeader.search` holds the search state, either {`type`:`off`} or {`query`:<text>,`type`:<text|jql|sjql>}. Opening a perspective on a live page applies it, along with the transformations, quick transformations, insertion-limit and infinite-loop close states.

In the secondary panel the two-panel button switches between 'all' and 'exclude'. With 'exclude' on a transformable spec, rows whose items are in the primary panel's current forest are hidden from the secondary grid, and the button appears active, with tooltip 'Show all items. Currently only showing items not presented in the left panel.' and label 'Show all items'. With 'all' or a spec that is not transformable the list is unfiltered and it has tooltip 'Hide items presented in the left panel. Currently showing all items.' and label 'Hide items'. Each change takes the focus off the active element.

The two-panel mode is remembered per browser, default `all`, and in a perspective under `secondary.panelHeader.twoPanelMode` (`all` or `exclude`; optional there). On the project page the widget starts in `exclude`; there the stored value is not read and changes made with the button last for that page load only, not being saved.

The generation-stopped banner follows the panel's stopped state. Absent state: banner closed. 'stopped': text 'We couldn't load the structure.', button 'Resume', enabled. 'resuming': text 'Generation is in progress...', button 'Resume' disabled. 'resumed': text 'Automation work was successfully resumed.', button 'Close' enabled. The state's icon follows these three states.

'Resume' sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/generation/resume` with body {`forestSpecs`:[<the panel's REST spec>]} (with `?loggedIn=<bool>` except in gadgets). The forests in the answer's `forestSpecs` go to the 'resuming' state and a poll is requested at once. A later poll that reports a forest as running or stopped turns 'resuming' into 'resumed' or back to 'stopped'. 'Close' in the 'resumed' state ends the state for this forest and its related forests, closing the banner, with no request. The button loses focus when clicked.

Only in the stopped state, and never in a gadget, on the issue page or on the Jira Software tab, the banner shows a 'More' link, which becomes 'Less' when expanded and reveals two paragraphs (about 300 characters) telling the user that automation or a transformation took too long so generation was paused, to review them and retry, and that the time limit can be set in the structure's settings. Below come the slowest generators.

On each poll result for the panel's spec, the stopped banner's details take `healthStatus.generatorTimes`: one row per generator, with the value as its share of the total of all `data` in percent with 2 decimals (for `data` 30 and 10: `75.00%` and `25.00%`), largest share first.

When a poll result for the panel's spec has `healthStatus.hitLimits` entries, a warning banner 'One or more Insert generators hit the insertion limit' opens, unless the user closed it. It has no action button. Its More/Less link (not in gadgets, issue page, Jira Software tab) reveals a short paragraph (about 250 characters) advising to edit the Insert generators to raise the limit or change the query, as results are incomplete until then, followed by a row per generator ordered by generator id, each with the entry's `data` (the limit reached). The count of entries is available to other parts of the widget.

When a poll result for the panel's spec has `healthStatus.infiniteUpdateGenerators` entries, a warning banner 'One or more generators cause an infinite update loop' opens the same way as the insertion-limit banner, with a paragraph (about 200 characters) saying that a likely cause is sorting over a formula which depends on forest position and an uncached value, and advising to review the listed generators. Its rows have an empty value.

Closing the insertion-limit or infinite-loop banner sets its own 'closed' flag, kept per panel in the browser and in a perspective (`ph.limits`, `ph.infinites`, boolean as text, default false). While the flag is set, the banner does not open automatically. Opening the banner by hand (from another part of the widget) clears the flag.

For the generators named in a poll result, the banner asks `POST /rest/structure/2.0/generation/generatorDescriptions` with a JSON array of generator ids (with `?loggedIn=<bool>` except in gadgets) and matches answers by `id` to read `description`. An empty or failed answer, or no generators in the result, closes the auto-opening banner and shows no details. The request is sent for each matching poll result that has generators; a poll result without the panel's spec changes nothing. A banner that opens automatically therefore opens only after that answer.

A generator details row has: the generator's description as an automation summary, re-rendered once if attribute metadata was still loading, its value, and a pencil. No pencil for a transient generator. With info `generatorConfigurationAllowed` the pencil has the title 'Edit this generator' and opens the generator edit dialog for that id; without, it is inert with title 'You don't have the required permissions to edit this generator'. The details show only while expanded and non-empty.

The query box is a growing one-line text area with a status icon on one end, a clear icon (tooltip 'Clear') on the other, and a placeholder per type: text 'Enter text query', jql 'Enter JQL query', sjql 'Enter S-JQL query', cql 'Search Confluence pages by title or CQL'. It is used for the source query (types text, jql, cql) and the search banner (text, jql, sjql). The placeholder is updated 50 ms after a type change.

For types jql and sjql, a non-empty text is checked 500 ms after typing stops, or 50 ms after a type change, with `GET /rest/structure/2.0/query/validate?q=<text>&type=<type>`. An answer for a text other than the current one is dropped. On answer `errors` non-empty the query stays as before and the error state is set. On answer `errors` empty or null the query value becomes the trimmed text, if different. A failed request changes nothing. Text and cql types are never validated; there the trimmed text is taken after the same 500 ms.

The status icon is a neutral quote mark for text and cql types, a success check for a valid jql or sjql query, and an error mark when the query has errors. Hovering the error mark shows each error as its own paragraph. Empty jql or sjql counts as valid and clears errors.
Clicking the clear icon empties the box and keeps focus in it.

Pressing Enter in the source query box applies the current text right away with no wait, then removes focus. It is not applied, and does nothing else, while the JQL autocomplete's list is displayed. No line break is ever inserted by Enter.

Only for type jql the box offers Jira's JQL autocomplete, loaded through Jira's search data (Jira's own REST) when the type becomes jql; it is removed on leaving jql and rebuilt when the box height changes. A parse problem reported by the autocomplete becomes the error state when none is set. Accepting a suggestion updates the query text.

While the box has focus and its content overflows, 100 ms after text or focus changes the clear icon is moved aside by the scrollbar's width, and with the caret at the end of the text the box scrolls to the bottom. Without focus the box collapses, and the icon returns.

The left of the header shows the selector button with the current source's icon and label, followed by the source's controls. For a structure: the name, a tooltip 'Current structure: <name>', and when the info says `isArchived` a lozenge 'archived'. With a null info the label is 'Unknown'. For a query the label is 'Text', 'JQL' or 'Pages' and the query box follows. For the clipboard: 'Clipboard'. For the project query: 'Current Project Issues'. Non-structure sources have no tooltip.

The structure parts of the header (name, archived mark, description button, favourite star) are updated 10 ms after the spec or info settles. While the info is not yet known or the source is not a structure, the description button, the star and the archived mark are hidden and the source's controls shown.

On the board page, when the structure info is null (a structure which does not exist or is not visible) the update of the favourite star fails with a script error after the name 'Unknown' has been shown, so no star is shown or refreshed (as the original does).

On the board page only, for a known structure, a star is shown after the name, reflecting `favorite` from the info. Clicking it sends `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/favorite` with {`favorite`:<the opposite>} as the page's shared favourites control does (see the `favorites` resource); on success the star follows the answer, its label changes on the button too, and the rest of the widget is told that the structure was updated. Other pages show no star.

The selector loads `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/list`, with `?anchorIssue=<id>` when the widget has a positive anchor issue, timeout 30 s, at install and each time the dropdown is opened (by mouse down on the closed selector, or keys `s`,`s`). There is at most one request in flight.

A failed list request schedules a retry after 1 s, 2 s and so on up to a cap of 20 s, but the guard for a load in progress is still set then, so no retry and no later load of the list happens during that page's life and the dropdown keeps what it had (as the original does).

Each list of the answer is mapped through `structures`, keeping ids found there with a positive id. It is cut to `maxItems` (10 when absent) entries, or one more when the list holds the structure being shown. An entry's label is its name, or `[<id>]` when nameless; names over 40 characters are cut to 37 plus `...`, and the full name is the tooltip. `containingAnchor` is used only when the answer's `anchorIssue` equals the widget's anchor issue. Counts of further items (`totalFavorites`, `totalContainingAnchor`) are not shown anywhere.

The dropdown has, top to bottom: a search box (placeholder 'Search Structure'); 'Structures with This Issue'; 'Recent Structures'; 'Favorite Structures'; 'Default Structures'; the structure search results (only while searching, when the sections before it are hidden); 'Tools'; and the Manage entry. A section with no items is not shown. 'Default Structures' is shown only when recents or favourites have no items in the answer. The structure being shown is left out of every section except favourites; a section left with nothing is dropped, but still counts as having items for that rule.

The sections are rebuilt only if the answer or the shown structure changed. The active (highlighted) entry after a rebuild is the existing active one, else the last hovered structure, else the first entry. Moving the mouse over an entry makes it the active one.

Each structure entry links to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`, but a plain click stays on the page: 10 ms later, if the panel state may change and no listener vetoes it, `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/recents?id=<id>` is sent (result ignored), the header shows the name and the panel's base spec is set to {`structureId`:<id>}, with the manage entry updated. If the current spec already equals that, only the recents request goes out. The click never loads the board page again.
On the board page in the primary panel, the first spec with a structure id also sends `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/recents?id=<id>` once per page load.

After a structure is picked in the dropdown, a 'Manage Structure' entry is added below Tools, opening `/secure/ManageStructure.jspa?id=<id>`. It is also added when the spec has a structure id plus other fields. It is not added for a spec that is only {`structureId`:<id>}, as on a plain page load, and it stays with the old target when another source than a tool is opened by other means; choosing an entry from Tools hides it (as the original does).

The 'Tools' section offers 'Text Search', 'JQL Query', 'Confluence Pages', 'Clipboard' with a badge of the clipboard's row count (shown when not 0), and 'Current Project Issues'. Choosing one, 10 ms later and if the panel state may change and nothing vetoes it, switches the source, focuses its input and hides the Manage entry. 'Current Project Issues' exists only on the project page. The Tools section is not offered on the issue page or the Jira Software tab, and all sections are hidden during a structure search.

'Confluence Pages' is available only when the Pages companion app is present, that is, the bootstrap config's `extensions` entry `com.almworks.structure.pages:pages-extension` has `licensed` true. The check is applied when the dropdown opens and its search box is empty, with the 500 ms delay of that box, so in the first half second of the first opening the entry may still be displayed. Without the companion app the entry is hidden.

Choosing a query source sets the spec to {`sQuery`:{`query`:<text>,`type`:<type>}} on each change of the valid query, with `query` empty when nothing was typed yet. Choosing 'Clipboard' sets {`type`:`clipboard`}. On the project page the project source sets its fixed query spec. Switching among text, JQL and Pages keeps the box and its text.

The selector follows the spec from outside: a structure spec selects no source; an `sQuery` with `projectQuery` selects the project source; another `sQuery` fills the text and selects its type; a spec with `type` selects that source.
On the project page the project source's spec is {`sQuery`:{`type`:`jql`,`query`:`project = "<KEY>"`,`projectQuery`:true}}.

A change of source or structure is refused when the panel's state cannot change right now. Before changing, the widget asks listeners, naming the panel, and any of them may veto. Both cases leave everything as it was, and the dropdown stays as the user left it.

With the dropdown open, the focus goes to its search box. Up and Down move the active entry among visible entries, stopping at the ends; with no active entry Down takes the first and Up the last. Enter clicks the active entry. Esc closes the dropdown and returns focus to the selector button; Tab closes it. Each of those keys goes no further. The key sequence `s`,`s` opens it; not in gadgets.

Typing in the dropdown's search box hides the sections and Tools; 500 ms after the last change `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure?limit=20&name=<url-encoded text>` goes out (timeout 30 s). With results: heading 'Structures Found' and each entry with its full name, linking as in the other sections. No results: heading 'Not found'. Failure: heading 'Search Error'. Emptying the box restores the sections, and Tools when available. Opening the dropdown resets the box. Answers arriving late are not dropped.

Ctrl+Alt+' (not in gadgets, on the issue page or Jira Software tab): if a text, JQL or Pages source is on and its box lacks focus, focus it. Otherwise switch the source: Text to JQL, JQL to Pages when the Pages app is present or else to Text, any other source to Text.
The widget can lock the selector to its structure (single-structure mode): the selector button is then aria-disabled.
The dropdown opens below the selector, or above when there is more room above; its height is limited to the room in the window.

The duplicates footer shows 'N rows with duplicates' with N from the panel's statistics `duplicateRowsCount` (0 if absent), a 'Filter' button (tooltip 'Hide items that have no duplicates'), a 'Pin' button (tooltip 'Pin selected item'), next and previous buttons ('Next duplicate', 'Previous duplicate') and the checkbox 'Mark duplicate rows'.
The 'Filter' button is a toggle telling the panel to show duplicates only. Any open or close of the footer, and its close control, turn it off.
The footer's Pin button runs the toggle-pin action, shows as pressed while an item is pinned, is disabled while transformations are disabled, and warns in automation editing mode.

Footer wording adapts to width, 10 ms after each layout change: when its content does not fit, it steps up a level, up to 3. Level 1 drops the Filter and Pin button texts. Level 2 shortens the count to only the number. Level 3 lays out the footer on several lines. It steps down when the room is larger than what was saved by stepping up. A hidden footer (width 0) is left alone.

When the panel can show duplicates, the footer's open state and the states of 'Mark duplicate rows' and 'Filter' (per panel, booleans as text, default false) are restored from the browser and from a perspective, where the paths are `<panel>.pf.duplicates.mark` and `<panel>.pf.duplicates.filter`. Restoring happens the first time the panel is visible; opening a perspective applies them to a live page.
The board toolbar sits above the grid wherever the page provides a place for it (board and project pages). It does not exist on the issue page or the Jira Software tab.

The toolbar's left side, in order: the split button 'Add' (tooltip 'Create a new item and add it to the structure'; its arrow: label 'Add items by type', tooltip 'Add new issues or other items to the structure, or search and add existing items'); 'Expand all' (tooltip 'Fully expand structure'), 'Collapse all' (tooltip 'Collapse all sub-items'), and an arrow 'Expand to a level...'; move up ('Move selected items up'), move down ('Move selected items down'), outdent ('Outdent selected items one level at a time'), indent ('Indent selected items one level at a time'); edit ('Edit focused item'), cut, copy, paste, remove, whose labels are 'Cut', 'Copy', 'Paste', 'Remove' and whose tooltips are 'Cut - mark selected items for moving to another place', 'Copy - mark selected items for copying to another place', 'Paste copied or cut rows after the currently focused item', 'Remove selected items and their sub-items from the structure (this does not delete issues or other Jira items)'; then 'Automation'.

The toolbar's right side, in order: 'Help' (menu), 'Share' (tooltip and label 'Share perspective'; hidden on the project page), 'Export' (menu), and the layout split button with an arrow 'Layout settings'.

Each toolbar button or menu entry performs a named grid action on the focused panel, or at widget level when no panel has focus. It takes its enabled state from that action: aria-disabled while unavailable, in which case a click does nothing; a split button's arrow goes with its main button. A toggle action shows as pressed or checked. Updates from a panel that does not have focus are ignored. Clicking a button removes focus from it.

The Add arrow opens a menu: 'New Issue', 'New Folder', 'New Memo', 'New Planning task', then, in order, the entry for pages and one per third-party item type, then in a section of its own 'Search & Add'.

The menu's 'New Page' entry, which starts creating a Confluence page row, is there when the Pages companion app is available (see claim selector-cql-entry). Without the app there is no such entry: the original's promotional entry for that app, which sends the user to the vendor's Marketplace listing, stays out of the replacement under the vendor identity rule.

For each entry of `externalGenericItemTypes` in `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`, the Add menu gets an entry labelled with `newItemTitle`, which starts creating an item of `type`. Entries are added once when the config has loaded, with their text HTML-escaped.

The expand arrow opens a menu with radio entries 'Level 1' to 'Level 8' and 'All Levels'. On opening, nothing happens if no panel has focus. Otherwise the focused panel's current level is checked, and each level is listed only when it is at most the maximum level of the forest, or the current one; 'All Levels' is always listed. Choosing an entry expands the focused panel to that level (0 for 'Level 1', up to 7 for 'Level 8', 10000 for 'All Levels').

The layout main button shows the current layout's icon and has the tooltip '<current>. Click to switch to "<next>".' with layout names 'Single Grid', 'Double Grid', 'Grid + Details', 'Grid + History', or a registered external panel's icon. Clicking it switches to the next layout and removes focus from the button.

The layout arrow's menu holds these sections. 'Layout': radio entries 'Single Grid', 'Double Grid', 'Grid + Details' (only when details are available) and 'Grid + History'. 'Layout Options': checkboxes 'Full Screen' and 'Mark Manual Adjustments'. 'Item Link Action': see claims item-link-*. Their behaviour is that of the layout management.

The toolbar's text shrinks by steps as it gets narrower: normal; no labels on the right side; also no 'Automation' label; and last the group edit, cut, copy, paste, remove is replaced by a single 'Edit' menu ('Edit focused item or change hierarchy') with entries 'Edit', 'Cut', 'Copy', 'Paste', 'Remove'. The first step whose measured width fits is used, and the last step if none fits; widths are measured with visible content, on start 200 ms after install, again when the help button or automation plus button appears, and the fit is rechecked on each window resize. Without permission to edit automation the 'Automation' label is not displayed.

When the config's `hideHelp` is absent, the 'Help' menu is shown with: 'Welcome to <product>', opening `secure/StructureWelcome.jspa` in the same window; 'Tips from your admin'; 'Documentation', a link in a new tab to the plugin's documentation; and 'About <product>', which opens the plugin's about dialog. The original's entry pointing at the vendor's community site is left out of the replacement. With `hideHelp` true the Help button, the menu and the first-use hint are not there at all.
'Tips from your admin' opens a Jira form dialog loaded from `/secure/StructureHelpDialog.jspa`. The entry is left out when the config's `hideHelpAdminTips` is true.

The first time the toolbar is shown in this browser with help available, a small popup at the Help button says 'Any questions?' / 'You can search for the answers here.' with a button 'Got it', which closes it. This is remembered in the browser at the moment it appears, without expiry, so it does not reappear.
The automation mode is remembered as `none` or `automation`, default `none`, in the browser and, in a perspective, at the top-level path `toolbar`. It is restored when storage is ready.

With `#devmode` in the URL fragment (as the only or a slash-separated part), or by the debug action at runtime, the toolbar adds developer buttons: 'Poll' (request a poll now), 'Upload Tree', 'Debug Mode' (toggle), 'Block Ajax' (toggle; turning off resumes sending), 'Exception', 'Error', 'Stop generation'. 'Stop generation' posts the focused panel's spec as `forestSpecs` to `POST /rest/structure/2.0/generation/stopIfRunning`, or `.../generation/stop` with Shift held. 'Upload Tree' has no effect from this toolbar.

The toolbar supports extra rows, each opened by a toggle button: at most one extra row shows at a time below the main one (opening another closes the open one), height 30 px, and its buttons are disabled while the focused panel is read-only. Nothing in the plugin itself uses this at present.
The 'Export' menu has 'Printable Page', 'Export to Excel (XLS)' and 'Export to Excel (XLSX)', each acting on the focused panel; no focused panel means nothing happens.

Exports send these parameters: `forestSpec`, the focused panel's REST spec as JSON text, for a structure with history shown using the shown version and no `transforms`, and in automation editing mode with `title` true and no `transforms`; `viewSpec`, the current view as JSON with each nameless column getting the name of its live column, or else `viewId`, the base view id, when there is no current specification; `expand`, the encoded expansion state; `clientFilter` when user filters exist; `signature`, the forest version signature or 0; `atl_token`; and, for Excel, `xlsx` true or false.

Excel exports open `/plugins/servlet/structure/excel` in the same window. 'Printable Page' opens `/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` in a window named per panel, so that a repeat replaces that window's content. Parameters go by GET unless the sum over them of (URL-encoded name length + URL-encoded value length + 2) exceeds 400; then by POST.

The items of web-item location `structure.export.menu` come from `exportLinks` of `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget` (those having `label`, `url` and `moduleKey`) and form a separate section after the built-in entries, in the order given. With none, there is no section. Each item shows `label`, an icon from `iconClasses` or the default export icon, `title` as tooltip, and opens in a new tab.

An export link's target is recomputed from the primary panel's REST spec (always the primary panel, whichever panel has focus), at every change of that spec. If the `url` holds `${forestSpec}`, its first occurrence is replaced by the spec's JSON, URL-encoded. Otherwise the URL gets a query parameter `forestSpec` with that JSON. With no spec the target is `#`.

The web item `export-structure-as-json` puts 'View as JSON', weight 1000, in location `structure.export.menu`, with the link `/rest/structure/2.0/forest/latest?s=${forestSpec}`. It is shown only when the server runs in development mode.

The 'Item Link Action' section (radio 'Open Details', 'Navigate to Item', 'Do Nothing') becomes active when the details panel is first initialized. Then `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/issueLinkAction` (timeout 30 s) loads `type`; it selects that radio only if none was picked meanwhile, and that does not send it back. A failed request only logs; nothing is selected.

Picking a radio sends `POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/issueLinkAction` with body {`type`:<showDetails|openIssuePage|doNothing>} through the upload queue. A failure only logs, and the selection stays.

The section and its entries are disabled, with a tooltip, in two layouts: with history shown 'Item link will always navigate to item in Grid + History layout'; with details shown 'Item link will always open item details in Grid + Details layout'; if both, the details text. Otherwise they are enabled and the tooltip is empty.

Clicking an item link in a grid, with history not shown: with details open, or in a non-primary panel, the link is not followed. Otherwise the choice decides: 'Open Details' opens the details panel and does not follow the link; 'Navigate to Item' follows it; 'Do Nothing' does not. With history shown this rule does not apply. The link loses focus in all those cases.
The first time a choice has a value after load, the statistic `issueDetails.issueLinkAction.<type>` is recorded once.
The section is hidden unless details are available in this widget (`showIssueDetails` configuration).

The 'Automation' toggle button (tooltip: a sentence of about 170 characters saying it turns on editing of generators and effectors and that added transformations are disabled meanwhile) turns automation editing mode on and off. It shows as pressed while on. It is disabled while history is shown or a new row is being edited. Keys `` ` `` and Shift+`` ` `` toggle it. After Enter on it focus stays on it.
When the structure gives neither `generatorConfigurationAllowed` nor `effectorConfigurationAllowed`, the Automation button's label is not displayed; the button itself stays.

An add button (tooltip of about 110 characters, accessible label 'Add an automation', saying that it adds a generator or effector under the focused item) appears beside the Automation button only when all hold: automation mode is on, the focused panel shows a structure, that panel is neither locked nor read-only, the structure allows configuring generators or effectors, and no new row is being edited. When a condition fails, an open menu from it closes and the button goes away.

The add button's menu lists one entry per generator kind known to the automation registry when generators are accessible, with that kind's icon, label and tooltip, then 'Effectors' (tooltip 'Create an effector under the current item') when effectors are accessible. Choosing an entry replaces the add button with a button named after the choice (the kind's action label or 'Effectors') and opens that list's menu at once. Closing that menu restores the add button, and when closed by Esc focus returns to it.

The list for a generator kind or for effectors shows the presets built for it by the automation dropdown. Choosing a preset with parameters adds it at once. Choosing one without opens the generator or effector edit dialog with the module key and the structure's id, and it is added on confirmation. Cancelling adds nothing.

New automation goes in by the focused row: when it is itself a generator or effector, right after it under the same parent. For any other row, as its first child. With no focused row, at the top of the root. `before` is the row following that position.

On adding, the grid shows a temporary row with a negative id at that spot right away. Its text is, for an effector, the effector's label; for a generator 'Filter by {0}', 'Insert {0}', 'Extend with {0}', 'Group by {0}', 'Sort by {0}' by generator type, where {0} is the matching preset's label or else the generator's.

A new automation is sent by `POST /rest/structure/2.0/item/create` through the upload queue with: `forest` the panel's versioned spec, `version` updated to the current one at sending; `items`.`version` the current items version; `parameters` {}; `rowId`, `under`, `after`, `before`; and `item` {`type`: `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-generator` or `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector`, `values`: {`moduleKey`, `params`}}. It waits while `under`, `after` or `before` is a temporary row or one with a pending upload. The answer's `itemId` is recorded and handed to the dialog's callback.

Dragging a new automation row whose creation has not been sent, or is waiting for a decision, changes its position in the pending request (and resets `parameters` to {}) and retries it, with `before` recomputed. Otherwise no move is made this way.

When a control marked for it (Pin, a filter or Save, transformation controls) is clicked while automation mode is on and history is not shown, the user is told: the first times, a popup at the Automation button says 'All additional structure transformations, such as sorting or filtering, are temporarily disabled when Automation Editing Mode is On.', with a button 'Got it' and the Automation button marked as in error till it hides. 'Got it' is remembered in this browser without expiry; afterwards the Automation button only flashes.

The Add Column panel has a text box (placeholder 'Search', at most 20 characters), the list, a 'Not found' line that shows only when a search finds nothing, and, on board and project pages but not in gadgets, the issue page or the Jira Software tab, a last entry 'Manage saved columns...'.

Groups are sorted by their order, then by title; presets are sorted by preset name. Each group that has presets gets a heading that cannot be selected, followed by its presets. Presets with no group, or a group that is not registered, go under the group that has no key. Column types whose metadata cannot be loaded contribute nothing. A preset with a description has it as tooltip.

Searching trims and lower-cases the text, and works on each change or key release. Group headings go away. Presets match when the name contains the text; the order is: exact name, then names starting with it, then the rest, in list order within each. Presets with the same column spec and name appear once. The selection stays when it is among the results, otherwise moves to the first result. Emptying the box brings the full list back.

Choosing a preset that is fully configured reports its column spec for adding. Choosing one that is not, or having no matching one, counts as cancelling. Choosing 'Manage saved columns...' reports that. Esc and Tab count as cancelling, also from the search box.

Each time the panel opens, the search box is emptied and takes focus, the selection is cleared and the list scrolls to the top. On closing, focus returns to where it was. The panel does not get narrower than at its first display.

In this list control Down selects the next visible item or, with none selected, the first. Up selects the previous visible item and does nothing with none selected or at the top. Enter chooses the selected item, and with none selected does nothing and lets the key pass. Moving the mouse over an item selects it, and clicking chooses it. The selected item is scrolled into view. Handled keys go no further.
Keys `s`,`q` open the Quick Actions box: a text box (placeholder 'Find <product> action...') with a list below it. It takes the keyboard focus. It closes when it loses focus (after 50 ms).

The box finds actions by name: an action's own title if it has one, else the text below for its grid action; an action with neither is not listed. The list is built once per page, from the widget's actions and those of the panel it first opened in; two actions with the same name raise an error. Names, each listed only if that action exists on the page: Toggle full screen mode; Undo; Redo; Toggle unresolved; Quick transformations; Toggle query; Switch panel; Hide all other panels; Show Secondary panel; Show Details; Show History; Add column; Select subtree; Deselect subtree; Select to the root; Collapse node; Expand node; Expand all; Collapse all; Expand next level; Collapse next level; Expand 1 level, Expand 2 levels ... Expand 8 levels; Next matching; Previous matching; Select; Select all; Copy; Cut; View thumbnails; Bulk change; Move item up; Move item down; Outdent item; Indent item; Delete subtree; Paste; Paste under; Edit; Create child; Create with dialog; Create under; Create; Create above; Create issue; Create folder; Search and Add; Add Confluence page; Edit next field; Edit previous field; Pin; Cancel issue edit; Cancel edit; Open issue; Actions drop-down; Assign issue; Edit issue; Assign issue to me; Comment issue; Manage views; Show shortcuts; Printable page; Export to Excel; Automation; Focus search; Toggle search filter; Swap panels; Run all effectors.

After a pause of 50 ms from a key release, with at least 2 characters typed, the list shows every action whose name contains the text, ignoring case, with the matching part in bold, the action's keyboard shortcut if it has one, and greyed if the action is currently unavailable. The first entry is selected. With fewer than 2 characters the list is empty.

In the box, Down and Up move the selection, wrapping at the ends and keeping it in view; Enter or a click runs the selected action, on the panel where the box was opened, closes the box and returns focus to where it was. An unavailable entry is run too (as the original does). Hovering an entry selects it.

The last search text of at least 2 characters, in lower case, is remembered in the browser. On the next opening it is filled in, selected and searched at once. Falling back below 2 characters clears what is remembered.

The pagination bar shows, left to right: back '<', page 1, a gap '…', the previous page, the current page, the next page, a gap '…', the last page, forward '>'. Page 1 shows when current index is above 1; the first gap above 2; the previous above 0; the next when below last-1 (0-based, with total pages N: index < N-1); the last when index < N-2; the last gap when index < N-3. Example: 10 pages, on the 5th: < 1 … 4 5 6 … 10 >.
The bar is shown only when there is more than one page: total pages = total records / page size, rounded up. Before the first answer it is hidden.

Back and forward go one page, stopping at the ends, and are disabled at those ends; forward also while the total is unknown. All buttons are disabled while loading, and the whole bar is disabled during that. Number buttons go to that page.

A page's records are requested once with offset = index × page size and count = page size, then cached with their scroll position, so going back shows them with no request and with the scroll where it was; a new page starts at the top. A failed page is not cached. Starting a new search goes to the first page and clears cache and scroll positions.

A paginated table posts to the URL given by its screen with content type `application/json; charset=UTF-8` and body {`startAt`,`maxResults`,`params`}. It reads `items` and `pagination.total`. It is used by the effector processes view, which claims the URL and columns.

Empty result: the message 'No records available'. Failure: the table's rows are removed and 'Failed to retrieve records from the server' is shown; the next load clears it. During a load the table and bar are in a loading state.

The loading spinner appears only if the wait lasts 500 ms, and once shown stays at least 500 ms; a wait that ends sooner shows no spinner at all. The control counts as busy until the spinner has gone.

The colour picker offers exactly, in this order: gray, blue, green, orange, red, purple. Initial value is the one given, or gray when that is missing or not one of these. A click on a colour selects it; with keyboard navigation turned on the colours can be tabbed to and Enter selects. While disabled nothing changes the value. Exactly one colour is marked as selected.

The tabbed dropdown is a searchable single-choice list with tabs at the top, used for choosing a saved column. The search placeholder is 'start typing...'. It opens on the tab holding the current value, or on the first tab. Clicking a tab shows that tab's options. Tab and Shift+Tab in the search box go to the next and previous tab, wrapping around.

When a tab has no options and nothing was typed it shows the text given by its screen, whose links open in a new window. When something was typed and nothing matches it shows 'No matches found', and Enter closes the dropdown.

Choosing an option sets the value and closes. When the screen installs a check, the dropdown closes first, the check runs, and the value is set only if it agrees. On closing, focus goes back to the trigger when there is one. A change of the value from outside updates the shown tab and choice. Near the window's edge the list shifts to stay on screen.

This tooltip appears 150 ms after the pointer or focus enters an element that has a tooltip text, and goes 300 ms after leaving. Moving from one such element to another, or onto the tooltip itself, within those 300 ms keeps it open, with the new content in the first case. Elements with no text show nothing. The text is HTML-escaped unless the element's text is declared to be HTML.
The tooltip opens 5 px below its element, left-aligned to it, moved left so that it stays inside the nearest scrolling container, and has a scroll limit to the room left in that container.
